findings.requirement: Preserve native recursive_triggers visibility and SQL name resolution. Audit failures must propagate and roll back all transfer effects; harmless guards must succeed.
findings.evidence: R2-F1 remains unresolved for SQLite's IN table shorthand. Initialize a temporary database with accounts ('red','a',100), ('red','b',20). Install: CREATE VIEW saved_mode AS SELECT 0 IN pragma_recursive_triggers AS recursive_triggers; CREATE TRIGGER native_guard BEFORE INSERT ON audit WHEN (SELECT recursive_triggers FROM saved_mode)=1 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'native guard'); END; Call transfer(path,'red','a','b',10,'new'). The candidate API and CLI succeed, committing balances 90/30, one receipt and one audit row. The same four writes on a fresh native connection raise IntegrityError and roll back completely. Changing the guard comparison to <>1 reverses the discrepancy: native execution succeeds while the candidate aborts. Schema-qualified IN main.pragma_recursive_triggers also reproduces it. The rewriter additionally breaks SELECT pragma_recursive_triggers.recursive_triggers FROM pragma_recursive_triggers NOT INDEXED: a harmless guard succeeds natively but the candidate raises OperationalError: no such column: pragma_recursive_triggers.recursive_triggers. These are remaining cases of the same incomplete SQL rewriting mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve native pragma visibility for IN table references and preserve source aliases before NOT INDEXED. Verify each form through native, API and CLI execution with both aborting and harmless guards.
